text.title: Futures jump as Anthropic's record IPO revives the AI trade after a five-day S&P slide
text.summary: Stock futures are sharply higher before the open, led by tech. Nasdaq 100 futures are up more than 2% and S&P 500 futures are up 1.2%, as the pricing of Anthropic's record IPO restores confidence in AI. That follows a rough stretch: the S&P 500 has fallen five straight sessions and is down 3.9% over five days. The VIX is easing, down 9.6% to 22.2. The 10-year Treasury yield is up 3 bp to 5.10%, the dollar is slightly softer, WTI crude is up 1.1% and gold is down 0.5%. The thread is risk appetite: AI sentiment is driving the rebound, while higher yields remain a headwind.
text.rates: The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10%, up 3 bp from the prior close and 5 bp below its one-month high. The 2-year is 4.80%, unchanged on Wednesday's close. Higher long-term yields raise the discount rate on future earnings, which typically weighs most on richly valued growth stocks, so the Nasdaq rally is working against that pressure. WTI crude is up 1.1% to $83.19 but remains about 20% below its one-month high. Gold is down 0.5% and has fallen 10.5% over the past month. The headlines don't explain today's moves in oil or gold, though Trump said the US will 'see what happens' with Iran after January 1.
text.breadth: Overseas trading was mixed. Japan's Nikkei rose 0.7%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 2.8%; the headlines don't explain the Hang Seng drop. In Europe, the Euro Stoxx 50 is up 0.2%, the FTSE 100 is down 0.4% and the DAX is down 0.1%. Europe is flat to slightly lower, so the US rally looks driven by the Anthropic story rather than by global momentum.
text.context: The S&P 500 enters today on a five-session losing streak, down 3.9% over five days and 5.6% below its one-month high. The Nasdaq is 8.5% below its one-month high. The Dow has fallen three straight sessions and the Russell 2000 is down 4.6% over five days. The VIX is down two sessions in a row but still 18.8% higher than five days ago, so today's bounce follows real stress.
text.takeaway: Market leadership has been concentrated in AI, so sentiment around the theme can move whole indexes in either direction. For diversified long-term investors, this is a reminder that short-term swings often reflect shifts in narrative rather than changes in long-run fundamentals.
text.talk: Stocks are set to bounce this morning after a rough week, helped by excitement over Anthropic's record IPO and a better tone toward AI. Futures gains don't always hold, and the market is still digesting a pullback and higher Treasury yields.

drivers.t: Anthropic and its co-founders raised a record $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement, and the shares debut on Nasdaq today. Gray-market indications point to a jump of more than 20% at the open. A strong debut tends to validate AI valuations and the capital still flowing into the theme. It lifts sentiment toward the large growth and chip names that dominate the Nasdaq, which explains why Nasdaq 100 futures (+2.0%+) lead the S&P 500 (+1.2%), the Dow (+0.6%) and the Russell 2000 (+0.6%). One caution: a deal this large also absorbs a lot of investor capital.
drivers.impact: Nasdaq futures lead, AI sentiment up

drivers.t: The rally follows a week in which AI leadership faltered. Nvidia's post-earnings drop weighed on the broader market in the prior session. Today Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, told staff to 'move forward' at her first all-hands since Jensen Huang's exit. Barclays calls the AI slowdown a correction rather than a collapse, but warns that if the AI trade unwinds, other pillars supporting the economy matter far less. That is why a single IPO can swing sentiment so much: markets are leaning heavily on this one theme.

Walmart raised its outlook and said store-fulfilled pickup and delivery were strong in its fiscal third quarter. Its CEO told CNBC the retailer aims to keep prices low despite soaring fuel costs. A raised forecast from the largest US retailer is a useful read on consumer resilience, and the fuel-cost remark shows how energy prices can squeeze margins. Even so, the stock is down about 1.0% premarket. The headlines don't say why, though the move may reflect high expectations or the cost pressure.

Palo Alto Networks is among the premarket movers after raising its outlook, citing the 'current threat environment and demand we see ahead of us.' Cybersecurity was a bright spot in the prior session, and the guidance extends that theme. Investors tend to reward software names that tie AI adoption to rising security spending. The headlines add that a top hedge fund links the surge in cyberattacks to the release of one AI model, and that the EU Commission confirmed an AI-assisted cyberattack on itself.

The dollar index hit a 19-month high of 103.974 overnight before slipping to 103.71. Deutsche Bank says it expects the dollar to stay firm into 2027 because of the AI boom, though it would turn if AI spending slows. A strong dollar tends to pressure commodities and multinational earnings. Separately, MarketWatch notes tech now screens cheap while defensive sectors like consumer staples look expensive, and CNBC's tracker shows family offices adding stocks while hedging AI risk with financials.

earnings.t: Management raised its outlook and cited strength in store-fulfilled pickup and delivery. It also flagged soaring fuel costs while pledging to keep prices low, which points to margin pressure.
